svg.title: Differenced VAR vs VECM
svg.desc: Differencing a cointegrated system discards the long-run relation; VECM restores it.
svg.text: Throw the long-run relation away with differencing, or restore it as error correction?
α gives the speed of return to equilibrium
the rank r of Π = αβ′
move together in the long run
Adding it when there is none
Spot and futures, the term structure
The spread keeps widening — no cointegration
The two stay together and the spread reverts
The spread returns to its mean — cointegrated
The level term Π is absent entirely
With the level term gone, nothing pulls toward equilibrium
If cointegration was really there, the estimates become inefficient
Factor Π into α and β′
α is the speed of return, β defines the equilibrium
r = 0 means a differenced VAR; r = n means the levels are already stationary
Differencing a cointegrated system discards the long-run information.
VECM brings that relation back as an error-correction term, pulling deviations home at speed α.
the rank is the number of relations
Next: correlation is not cointegration — the basis of pairs trading.
